analyzed_vuln.description: In ff_jpegls_decode_picture(), the post-processing shift path for >8-bit samples uses `uint16_t *src = (uint16_t *)s->picture_ptr->data[0]` and then iterates `for (x = 0; x < w; x++) src[x] <<= shift;` where `w = s->width * s->nb_components`. This assumes the decoded frame buffer is tightly packed 16-bit samples for all components. For crafted JPEG-LS streams (as reached via ff_mjpeg_decode_sos), decoder state can make this assumption false (mismatched pixel format/layout/stride vs bits/components), so `src[x]` dereferences invalid memory and crashes (UBSan SEGV at line 541). Root cause is missing validation/consistency checks before 16-bit in-place transform in ff_jpegls_decode_picture().
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Input must be parsed as lossless JPEG-LS (`s->ls` true) and reach ff_jpegls_decode_picture() from ff_mjpeg_decode_sos(). The bitstream must drive parameters so the `shift` block executes and the `s->bits > 8` branch is taken, while frame buffer layout is inconsistent with `width * nb_components` 16-bit linear access (e.g., malformed headers causing inconsistent component/format state). Then the loop at jpeglsdec.c:541 reads/writes out-of-bounds and crashes.
